subject.title: [Feature]: deterministic context injection for bootstrap files and session-type filtering

question: Should OpenClaw expose a first-class bootstrap selector and dynamic command-expansion contract for sessions, and where should the command-execution boundary live?
rationale: The remaining request changes public config/API behavior and would let workspace prompt files trigger command execution, so automation cannot safely choose the long-term product and security boundary.

options.title: Narrow selector API first
options.body: Add a small maintained tier or selector contract for session-scoped bootstrap inclusion and defer command expansion until a separate security design is approved.

options.title: Plugin hook only
options.body: Keep core bootstrap loading limited to safe built-in files and route dynamic per-session context through documented hooks or plugins.

options.title: Full command expansion
options.body: Pursue bootstrap !command expansion only with explicit sandboxing, provenance, opt-in behavior, and upgrade-safe docs/tests.

recommendation.title: Narrow selector API first
recommendation.body: Add a small maintained tier or selector contract for session-scoped bootstrap inclusion and defer command expansion until a separate security design is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for bootstrap resolution, session filtering, and date-time prompt policy points to steipete, and the decision crosses product/API and security boundaries.
